entries.name: com.apple.universalaccessAuthWarn
entries.note: Accessibility authorization warning. BifrOSt gates the same capability by the manifest `accessibility` permission (events service) and the per-app Universal Access policy.
entries.ready_note: Control of the computer through accessibility is consented to up front: an app must hold the `accessibility` permission in its manifest (shown by the App Store at install), the events service refuses every call without it, and a per-app policy can deny zoom, screen reader, keyboard or pointer features. There is no separate start-up warning dialog because there is no pre-authorised list to re-confirm.

entries.name: com.apple.universalaccesscontrol
entries.note: Accessibility settings and zoom; no per-app universal access policy; built 2026-10-17: per-app policy (universal_access_control service, a11y_app_denials pref) denies zoom, screen_reader, keyboard or pointer to one app; tests shell::services::universal_access_control::tests. The Settings editor for the policy is not built, so only the pref and service read it.
entries.ready_note: The per-app policy is a model with the pref round trip and the service answers (allowed, denied) per calling app; global settings still decide whether a feature is on. The Settings page that edits the policy is not built, so apps can be denied through the pref only.

entries.name: com.apple.universalaccessd
entries.ready_note: The accessibility models (ax, captions, braille cell translation) run in the shell, and the braille service answers translation requests. The only part not built is a Braille display driver, which needs hardware.
entries.note: rule: accessibility models; the `braille` service translates text to Braille cells (no display driver yet)

entries.name: com.apple.usermanagerhelper

The sheets in shell/forms.rs ask for the name, the full name and the password, and a new or changed password is typed twice before privd receives it (shell/users_page.rs). The directory and console services answer the account list read-only.

entries.name: com.apple.voicebankingd
entries.note: Records voice samples and adapts speech to the speaker. Built: the sample store (voice_banking service, a11y_voice_bank pref: one good sample per script phrase, bad rates and lengths refused, progress) and, 2026-10-22, speaker measurement: ui voice_profile.rs measures pitch (mean and range by autocorrelation), pace (syllable peaks per second) and loudness from recorded PCM, merges them per bank, and VoiceProfile::apply sets the rule-based synthesiser's pitch multiplier and rate; the service keeps each phrase's profile (a11y_voice_profiles) and answers voice(). Missing: the app must upload the audio itself (the shell keeps metadata and measurements only) and training a personal voice (timbre, phoneme shapes), which needs a trainable speech model; speech.rs has no speaker adaptation beyond pitch and rate.
entries.ready_note: The sample store, the profile analysis on synthetic voices (pitch, pace, loudness, silence/noise refusal, decimation), merging, the synthesiser mapping and the service's profile storage are tested.

entries.name: com.apple.ContainerMigrationService
entries.note: Migrates app data containers when the OS upgrades. Built: per-container format version file, resumable non-downgrading migration steps, and (2026-10-22) a copy-on-upgrade snapshot that is restored when a step fails (migrate_safely) and migrate_all over a containers root that reports each app's result without one failure stopping the rest. Missing: the updater (packaging/arch/recovery, updated) calling migrate_all after an OS install, and the concrete per-app migration steps (none exist yet, no app has bumped its format).
entries.ready_note: Version file, step chain, resume, downgrade refusal, snapshot/restore on failure, no snapshot for an up-to-date container and migrate_all are tested.

entries.name: com.apple.Kerberos.kcm
entries.note: Kerberos credential cache manager. The krb5 library stores caches itself (FILE, DIR, KEYRING); SDK gss_krb5 names caches and krb5_client runs kinit and klist. No KCM daemon.
entries.ready_note: Credential caches are kept by the Kerberos library in files, directories or the kernel keyring, not by a cache daemon: kinit and klist run from the SDK (krb5_client.rs, krb5 package) against the cache an app names (gss_krb5.rs), and a cache can be copied between names. KCM: names are parsed so a cache served by another system daemon can still be used. BifrOSt runs no KCM server.

entries.name: com.apple.endpointsecurity.endpointsecurityd
entries.note: Built 2026-10-17: bifrost_core::endpoint_security reads fanotify records, matches them to subscriptions with path muting, collects authorization answers (one deny denies, a missing answer allows at the deadline) and builds the kernel reply. Wired 2026-10-17: bifrost-privd owns the fanotify descriptor (marks the real file systems from /proc/self/mountinfo, resolves paths from /proc/self/fd, never reads contents) and queues events per subscription; the shell service endpoint-security relays them to apps and answers, only for first-party system apps whose manifest declares entitlements = ["endpoint-security"]; bifrost_app::endpoint_security is the app client.
entries.ready_note: The path is real from the kernel feed to the app: privd (root) feeds the model from fanotify and queues events, the shell service checks the manifest entitlement on every call and relays poll/answer through privd, and a subscription ends when its app stops running. Only the shell may call privd's endpoint_security methods. Host tests drive the hub, the wire types, the entitlement rule and the shell service with a fake backend; the fanotify calls themselves (fanotify_init, fanotify_mark per file system, the read loop) cannot run in a host test and need a Midget run as root. Not done: the Settings > Privacy list of apps that hold the entitlement, and the manifest entitlement is not yet in app_policy::ENTITLEMENT_NAMES (the service reads the manifest itself).
